title: #BIS-easiness of Boolean log-supermodular counting CSPs
formal: For every fixed finite family F of functions \(f:\{0,1\}^{r_{f}}\to \mathbb{Q} _{\ge 0}\) satisfying \(f(x\lor y)f(x\land y)\ge f(x)f(y)\) for all x,y, is #\(\mathrm{CSP}(F)\) approximation-preserving reducible to #BIS?
definitions: Arity \(r_{f}\) is a nonnegative integer fixed with \(f; \lor\) and ∧ act coordinatewise. A #\(\mathrm{CSP}(F)\) instance consists of finitely many Boolean variables and a list of constraints, each naming a function in F and an ordered tuple of variables of its arity; repeats in a tuple are permitted. Its value Z is the sum over all Boolean assignments of the product of all constraint values. Function tables are fixed nonnegative rationals, not part of the instance. #BIS counts all independent vertex sets of a finite simple bipartite graph. An approximation-preserving reduction is a randomized oracle algorithm which, on an instance I and rational \(\varepsilon \in (0,1)\), returns a relative \((1\pm \varepsilon )\) estimate of Z with probability at least \(3/4\) using time polynomial in |I| and \(1/\varepsilon\). Its oracle calls request relative approximations to #BIS with inverse tolerances polynomially bounded in |I| and \(1/\varepsilon\). Oracle failure probabilities may be reduced to an inverse polynomial by independent repetitions; the reduction’s overall correctness guarantee includes them. If \(Z=0, a\) valid relative estimate is exactly zero. Reduction polynomials may depend on the fixed family F. The oracle is an approximation oracle, not exact counting.

context_blocks.text: Exact finite-domain counting CSPs already have major dichotomy theorems. Approximate counting has a different landscape, and log-supermodularity is one of its central boundaries. This question asks whether that whole Boolean region reduces to the benchmark problem #BIS.

Some log-supermodular functions cannot be represented by the standard implication-and-unary gadgets. That algebraic obstruction does not refute an approximation-preserving reduction, which is a more general notion. The target is this computational gap, not a claim that every counting problem has an established three-way classification.

why: A broad missing piece in the classification of approximate counting and weighted constraint satisfaction.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated proposition or its logical negation, preserving the quantifiers, model and guarantees. Conditional results settle only their conditional claims. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof-assistant-checked proof of the full target.

progress.text: The survey separates log-supermodular expressibility from #BIS-easiness, and leaves the general computational classification open.
The classification isolates the log-supermodular approximation region but does not collapse it to #BIS by a general AP-reduction.
